response.passage: Last Sunday, on October 14th, our nature club organized a bird-watching walk at the Okhla Bird Sanctuary. Mr. Sharma, our biology teacher, led the group of 12 students through the marshy trails. We were instructed to remain silent because sudden loud noises frighten the migratory birds away from their feeding grounds. While walking, we spotted a Kingfisher perched on a dry branch. Later, we saw a group of Painted Storks near the water edge. Rohan, who had brought his heavy binoculars, struggled to keep up with the pace of the group. By noon, the heat became intense, and we decided to head back to the main gate. Mr. Sharma explained that the sanctuary attracts many species during winter because the wetlands provide abundant fish for the birds. We learned that observation requires patience, as birds are sensitive to human presence. As we exited, we saw a local fisherman casting his net, unaware of the delicate balance of the ecosystem. It was a tiring but enlightening experience for everyone involved.
response.summary: A group of students visited the Okhla Bird Sanctuary with their teacher to observe migratory birds. They learned that silence is essential for bird-watching and that the sanctuary's wetlands are vital for the birds' survival.
